text:
anya (PM): Heads-up — ACME flagged a launch requirement: guaranteed 99th pctl latency for dedicated reserved pool during >=10k QPS sustained bursts for up to 3 minutes. They're asking for a firm SLA + credit if we miss.

sam (eng): whoa. do they mean hard guarantee even during cross-region failover?

mei (cs): they said within-region only for GA, but they want fallback behavior documented for multi-region. they want us to surface prewarm state and expected degradation.

ravi (eng-sre): important edge cases: if tenant burst > pool headroom and autoscale lag applies, we either preempt best-effort tenants or fail with 429s. need policy for preemption + soft cap.

anya (PM): propose: carve a small prewarm window (30s) + a soft spillover band (10% of pool) for 90s, after that preempt lower-tier tenants. ACME wants no silent throttles — they want observable fallback + credits.

jordan (design): UI/console asks: show per-tenant "prewarm state" and a live estimated SLA risk meter. simple green/yellow/red for the window.

sam (eng): spec details we need to finalize: 1) admission rule for bursts (token-bucket vs instantaneous qps), 2) preempt order (LRU sessions? priority labels), 3) retry hints to client, 4) metric labels for billing credits.

ravi (eng-sre): add: circuit-breaker behavior when spillover crosses threshold. sequence: emit event -> switch to best-effort -> preempt -> escalate to oncall. Ops-bot can post the event to #incidents.

ops-bot: automated: reserve-pool "acme-ga" prewarm=30s soft-band=10% spillover-action=preempt low_prio_label=backfill

mei (cs): ACME legal asked about SLA penalty math. we should propose a credit formula tied to 99th pctl miss > X ms for >Y minutes. i'll take draft to them if we have numbers.

anya (PM): launch criteria draft (for this feature):
- implementation: admission + preempt + console indicators + billing metric emitted
- load test: pass 3 sustained 10k-QPS 3-minute bursts in staging without 99th pctl > target
- SLO doc: fallback behavior and credit calc reviewed by legal
- oncall playbook + alerting mapped to incident severity

sam (eng): tech constraints: our autoscaler has ~45s median scale-up latency under current infra. prewarm needed. alternative is faster scale path for reserved pools (warm standby nodes) but that's costy. need product decision on cost vs guarantees.

anya (PM): two options for product decision: A) keep current autoscale + prewarm window + soft band (lower cost) B) introduce warm-standby reserved nodes for guaranteed latency (higher committed cost, higher SLA). Need go/no-go from GTM and finance.

mei (cs): ACME is willing to pay a premium for B, but wants pricing and a short pilot first.

ravi (eng-sre): ops impact: B requires dedicated preallocated capacity and a new billing label. also changes failure modes (less preemption but higher wasted capacity if unused).

jordan (design): minimal console changes for A, larger UX for B (new license tier + toggle + cost estimator).

anya (PM): action items:
- sam: prototype soft-band admission + preempt logic and add metric tag "sla_impact_candidate" — due EOD Friday
- ravi: draft oncall playbook and incident automation wires for preempt events — due Mon
- mei: pricing ask to finance + ACME pilot terms draft — due Tue
- jordan: mockups for prewarm indicator and SLA risk meter — due Wed

sam (eng): ack. i'll push a PoC branch and ping this thread when ready.

mei (cs): i'll let ACME know we have a pilot path and ask for their pilot dates.

anya (PM): ok — if PoC shows we can't meet 99th pctl with A, we'll table that to B and get a budget decision. please keep notes in the doc: /docs/dedicated/ga-handshake-acme (draft).

ravi (eng-sre): one more edge-case: sustained burst coinciding with regional infra degradation. propose a clause: SLA is within-region and does not apply during platform-wide incident windows. legal needs wording.

mei (cs): noted. will loop legal.

ops-bot: reminder: run staging load test job "acme-10k-burst" nightly this week.

anya (PM): thanks all. short sync Thursday 10am to review PoC results and decide A vs B. :thumbsup:
